about: How BlockMD feels to use, not just whether features work — the gap that let the 0.1.6 app menu ship with no hover highlight and a 0.2 s lag on every section switch. Categories are the ones a professional desktop-app QA pass covers: interaction states, responsiveness budgets, keyboard-only use, input methods (IME), visual regression, window sizes and display scaling, performance and memory, accessibility. Budgets come from the RAIL model (web.dev/rail: respond to input within 100 ms, animate within one 16 ms frame, 50 ms task chunks) and WCAG 2.2 AA (w3.org/TR/WCAG22). Same statuses as notion.json; every 'must' is checked by `npm run parity` in the real app and gates releases.

features.feature: Every clickable thing lights up under the pointer within 50 ms — top bar, app menu (all levels), page style menu, block menu, slash menu, format toolbar, find bar, drag handle, code language button and menu, emoji picker, toggle arrow, table of contents — and disabled items don't; highlighted text stays readable (4.5:1)
Every control reached with the keyboard shows where the focus is
App menu: moving between sections switches the submenu at once (under 100 ms); heading diagonally into the open submenu keeps it; resting on another section switches after at most 0.5 s
Typing in a 3,000-block document: each keystroke on screen within 50 ms (95th percentile), no frozen frame over 100 ms
A 1 MB, 10,000-block file opens within 3 s and saves byte-identical within 1 s
Opening and editing 30 documents in a row doesn't leak: memory, DOM nodes and event listeners return to where they were
App menu by keyboard: F10 or Alt opens it, arrows move and open submenus, Enter runs, ← goes back, Esc closes and returns to the text
Slash menu, block menu, emoji picker, code language menu and find: arrows, Enter and Esc work, and Esc puts the caret back where it was

The caret is drawn (it blinks on screen), the right height, not hidden under anything, readable (3:1), and text goes in exactly where it is — right after launch, Ctrl+N, Ctrl+O, Open Recent and dropping a file (no click needed), empty document, paragraphs (click, Home, ←), headings, lists, tasks, quotes, callouts, code, tables, toggles, columns, beside inline code / links / equations, after Enter, Backspace, Esc, undo, Chinese input, zoomed, dark mode
Chinese/Japanese input: the Enter that confirms a candidate never also makes a new block, picks a slash-menu item or emoji, jumps in find, replaces, or submits a link or equation
Text typed through an input method lands once, in the right place, and is saved exactly — in an empty line, a list, a heading, and inside a toggle
Only the ASCII : opens the emoji picker; the full-width ： a Chinese keyboard types does not (as in Notion). (In Chinese mode / still types /, so the slash menu needs nothing.)
features.note: Owner's decision (2026-09-29): after ： the keyboard is still in Chinese mode, and the emoji word would be turned into Chinese candidates — the picker would get in the way. Keep the English punctuation as the trigger.

features.feature: Screens look the same as the approved screenshots (document light and dark, app menu, slash menu, block menu, toolbar, find, table of contents, narrow window) — any unapproved change fails, with a diff image
At the smallest window (560 × 420) nothing is cut off, overlaps or scrolls sideways, and every menu stays on screen
At 150 % and 200 % display scaling the layout holds and icons are sharp
Text is readable: WCAG AA contrast (4.5:1, large text 3:1) in light and dark — document, top bar, status bar, menus
Deliberately faint text reaches AA too: shortcut hints, word count, code language label, finished tasks, inline code's red, a callout's [! ]
features.note: Owner's decision (2026-09-29): keep Notion's faint greys. The list is NOTION_FAINT in scripts/parity-feel.mjs; everything else must pass AA.

features.feature: Every control has a name a screen reader can say, and menus announce themselves as menus
